stem.en: Which statement about displacement is true?

feedback.en: It is zero whenever the object ends where it started.

text.en: Its magnitude can be more than the distance travelled.

feedback.en: Displacement joins the start to the end, the shortest way, so it can never be longer than the path.

text.en: Its magnitude is less than or equal to the distance travelled.

feedback.en: Right. It is equal when the object never turns back, and less when it does.

text.en: Its magnitude is always less than the distance travelled.

feedback.en: Not always. If the object never turns back, the two are equal.

explanation.en: The magnitude of displacement equals the distance travelled when the object moves in one direction without turning back. It is less when the object turns back. It is never more.

hints.en: Think of a run with no turning back, and a run that ends at the start.
